column2: On the authority of Abū Burdah, from his father, Abū Mūsā al-Ashʿarī (may Allah be pleased with him), that the Prophet ﷺ sent him to Yemen, and he asked him about drinks that were made there. He said: “And what are they?”
He said: “Al-bitʿ and al-mizr.” Abū Burdah was asked: “What is al-bitʿ?”
He said: “Honey wine, and al-mizr is barley wine.” He said: “Every intoxicant is unlawful.” Reported by al-Bukhārī.
The printed text reads كل فسكر حرام, evidently a misprint for كل مسكر حرام (“every intoxicant is unlawful”).
Baʿathahu (“sent him”): dispatched him to Yemen. Wāliyan: as governor.
ʿAn al-ashribah (“about drinks”): about what is made for drinking as an intoxicant. Nabīdh: a juice [left to steep].
(Note) Barley wine is what is now called beer, which is made for drinking.
The prohibition of consuming any intoxicant whatsoever, whether from grape juice or anything else.
A muftī may answer the questioner with more than he was asked if he knows that the addition is of benefit.
The cause of the prohibition is intoxication; what this requires is that every intoxicant is unlawful.
Names do not change realities.

This hadith tells us and guides us to the fact that whatever is made for drinking and is intoxicating is unlawful to drink, in small or large amounts; its use is unlawful, and its sale and handling are unlawful, of whatever kind it is and by whatever name it is called. May Allah protect us from that.
And whoever is appointed over any region of the land should ask about whatever of its people's affairs is unclear to him,
and about the products made in that land, so that he has clear insight into their ruling, avoids error and acts correctly. May Allah grant us and every official success in what is right.
Among what has been said in censure of those who drink intoxicants:
The coward of the tribe says when drunk, / having drunk the red wine: “Is there anyone to duel?”
When drunk he is Qays, Ibn Maʿdī and ʿĀmir; / but sober, you find him like an old woman.
Another poet:
I have left nabīdh to the people of nabīdh, / and now drink pure water.
I saw that nabīdh humbles the mighty / and withers handsome, radiant faces.
If it is not permitted to the young, / what excuse is there for it when grey hair appears?
